learning_objectives: Understand what Artificial Intelligence is, why it is needed, its fundamental principles, major types, capabilities, applications, and basic concepts of intelligent systems.
syllabus:
Week 1: Fundamentals of AI

Cover:
1. What is Artificial Intelligence?
2. Why do we need AI?
3. History and evolution of AI
4. Fundamental principles of AI
5. Characteristics of AI systems
6. Types of AI: Narrow AI, General AI, and Super AI
7. AI capabilities
8. How AI systems work at a basic level
9. Major areas of AI
10. Common applications of AI
11. AI vs traditional programming
12. Basic intelligent-agent concept
13. Advantages and limitations of AI
14. Exactly 2 real-world AI examples

Do not include Ethical AI, AI bias, fairness, responsible AI, or AI ethics in Week 1.
slides: Create clear and visually engaging slides with short points, diagrams, simple examples, and concept comparisons. Avoid excessive text. Keep the content suitable for beginners.
script: Create a simple lecture script that explains every slide clearly. Use conversational explanations, examples, questions for students, and smooth transitions. Avoid unnecessary technical jargon.
assessment: Use conceptual MCQs, short-answer questions, discussion questions, and simple application-based questions covering the fundamentals taught in the chapter.
overall: Week 1 must be strictly about Fundamentals of AI. Start from the basic question "What is AI?" and gradually introduce its principles, characteristics, types, capabilities, working, areas, and applications. Include exactly 2 real-world examples only. Do not introduce Ethical AI or related topics in this week. Keep the course beginner-friendly and suitable for B.Tech/M.Tech students.
